correctness.rationale: The normalized polar bodies and one shared Haar U are explicit: w_Q=2S and w_O=2M_R. The three given r_i form an orthonormal determinant+1 frame; r_1+r_2+r_3=(1,1,1), giving the stated 60-degree rotation. The marginals E[S]=3/2 and E[M_R]=(3√2/(2π))(π/2−θ) are consistent with direct spherical integration. For aligned axes, the winner-chart Jacobian and two elementary double integrals give E[S M_0]=1/3+2√2/π. For the rotated axes, all 48 sign/winner configurations were generated from exact halfspace inequalities, and 24 full-dimensional cones survive: A6 triangular, B12 triangular, C6 pentagonal. Their exact spherical areas and edge corrections follow from Gauss–Bonnet and the bilinear sphere Laplacian boundary formula; summing gives E[S M_1]=11/18+(2+√2/3)/π−4θ/(3π). The covariance formulas result by subtracting E[S]E[M_R] and multiplying by four. Independent cone enumeration found the same 24 chambers and total area 4π, the separate cone edge sums matched the exact expression to ~1e−15, and double numerical integration independently reproduced the aligned elementary terms. Independently developed exact rational bounds (not floating point) enclose aligned covariance in [−0.052539217903,−0.052539217813] and rotated covariance in [0.027071539660,0.027071539726], proving strict signs; independent full-sphere quadratures at four resolutions converge to those values. These finite calculations corroborate, rather than replace, the exact geometric integration argument. No claim of a continuum phase diagram, rotational maximum, or asymptotic generalization was assessed.
residual_risks: The decisive exact chamber decomposition relies on a nontrivial finite integer-cone enumeration; independently enumerated rays, types, areas and edge terms corroborate its exhaustive constraints, but no separate formal Lean/expert proof is claimed.
Independently sampled quadrature is not an exhaustive proof of the continuum formulas; analytic sphere Laplacian identity, exact halfspace geometry and rational sign enclosure provide the proof.
Some intermediate symbolic angle simplifications use standard exact inverse-cosine identities, not a new general angular classification.

value.rationale: The cube and its polar octahedron are a canonical 3D dual regular-solid pair with extensively studied separate width distributions. Their shared-view directional-width covariance is a natural stereological joint invariant; two bodies have exactly the same individual width laws when one rotates, yet the actual coupling reverses sign. The chosen relative 60-degree turn about the body diagonal is the symmetry-distinguished halfway rotation to the 120-degree cubic symmetry, not a freely tuned random angle. Providing both exact elementary constants and a finite exact spherical-chamber mechanism exhibits geometrically substantive information that cannot be extracted from individual moments. A future study of oriented joint widths or paired projections could use the explicit opposite-sign benchmark; no global phase theorem or paper-size extrapolation is needed for this independently motivated fact. This is not a trivial normalization, substitution, or table entry.
residual_risks: The finding is a two-orientation benchmark, not a classification of the complete rotation group.
The sign change follows from quantitative oriented integration, not a conceptual invariant for all regular polar pairs.
